one_month_reasoning: Inside the window ending 2026-11-05: Ericsson Q3 on 15 Oct 2026 (source 6) and Nokia Q3 on 22 Oct 2026 (Q2 6-K, source 1). Management guided Q3 comparable OP 'broadly similar to quarter two' (Q2 EUR 434m), net sales +3% to +7% q/q, and Mobile Infrastructure gross margin 'closer to 44% to 46%' (call, source 2), so a headline surprise is likely small. What moves the stock: AI & Cloud order intake after Q2's EUR 2.8bn, which management said is lumpy ('we should not expect this level of intake every quarter'); whether 'somewhat above the midpoint' of EUR 2.1-2.6bn is kept; and FCF, already guided to the low end of 55-75% conversion (sources 1,2). Q2 showed the stock can fall on in-line results (-5.4% on report day, 23 Jul, Twelve Data closes, source 13). No Nokia 6-K since 8 Sep (source 4); the FWA sale to Inseego closed on 1 Oct and is immaterial (source 5). Today's +6.3% (10.20 to 10.84) has no Nokia filing behind it, so I take no drift from it. I have no directional edge for Q3, so the ladder is a lognormal with median $10.76 (spot less a small vol drag) and sigma 0.1876 = 3-month realized vol 65.2% x sqrt(21/252), from my own computation on Twelve Data closes (source 13). That gives P(>=10.84) = 0.48. The Infront Q3 consensus I quoted in round 1 is no longer used: the nokia.com PDF returned 403 on re-check. FX: the ADR moves about 1:1 with EUR/USD (ECB 1.1269, source 10).

fair_value.method: Blend of 45% P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 EUR 0.3932 x 18.9x = EUR 7.43 = $8.37), 25% SOTP on 2028E (NI NOPAT x 24.3x + MI NOPAT x 13.6x - common + net cash = EUR 8.01/sh = $9.03) and 30% DCF at Oct-2027 (2028 FCF EUR 2.18bn = 70% CMD conversion, +6%/yr to 2032, g 3%, cost of equity 9.54% -> EUR 6.99 = $7.88). Blended $8.39, 23% below the $10.84 brief price (a 6 Oct intraday price from the run brief; the official 6 Oct close was $10.975, StockAnalysis NOK history); implied 18.2x FY2027 consensus EPS EUR 0.41.

methods.inputs: Valued at Oct-2027: FCF 2028E EUR 2,183m (70% x OP 3,119m), +6%/yr to 2032 (2,314/2,453/2,600/2,756), terminal g 3%, discount 9.54%, mid-year timing (t = 0.73..4.73). PV FCF EUR 9.58bn + PV TV 28.21bn = EV 37.79bn + net cash 2.78bn = EUR 40.56bn / 5,801.9m = EUR 6.99 = $7.88

bear.story: AI & Cloud orders prove pulled forward (management already calls intake lumpy), supply and memory costs cap NI margin near 10-11%, MI flat: OP 2027E EUR 2.45bn, 2028E EUR 2.7bn (CMD low end). NTM EPS = 0.25 x 0.3217 + 0.75 x 0.3533 = EUR 0.3454 x 15x (telecom cohort: ERIC 13.6x, HPE 14.5x, CALX 15.1x) = EUR 5.18 = $5.84. AI premium gone; below the thesis-break level.

base.story: My bottom-up path: FY26 'somewhat above midpoint', NI +15% in 2027 at a 13% margin, MI ~EUR 1.56bn, 2028E OP EUR 3.1bn. NTM EPS EUR 0.3932 x 21.2x = EUR 8.34 = $9.39. 21.2x is halfway between my peer-justified 18.9x and today's 23.5x on FY27 consensus: I assume the valuation gap closes about half-way in 12 months, because NOK has held an AI-optical premium all year and its IP/optical peers trade at 21-41x.

bull.story: Consensus path or better: FY2027 EPS EUR 0.41 met and 2028E EUR 0.46 (OP ~EUR 3.5bn, above the CMD top end) as AI & Cloud backlog converts and NI margin reaches 15-17%. NTM EPS 0.4475 x 27.5x (IP/optical-systems median) = EUR 12.31 = $13.87.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E (calendarised, one source: S&P Global consensus via StockAnalysis, prices 6 Oct 2026): 11.0x (RBBN) to 41.0x (ANET); quartiles 13.6x / 17.2x / 26.4x. Core telecom and IP/optical systems subset (ERIC, CSCO, CIEN, ANET, HPE, CALX, ADTN, RBBN) median 14.8x. Uncalendarised (raw fiscal-2027 figures, the supervisor's basis) the same 11 peers give a median of 16.0x or 18.6x, depending on whether June-year-end EXTR and VIAV use FY2028 or FY2027. comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18.9x NTM P/E is inside the range and 10% above the 17.2x median. NOK trades at 23.5x CY2027 consensus EPS EUR 0.41 ($10.84 brief price, a 6 Oct intraday price / (0.41 x 1.1269); 23.8x at the $10.975 close), a 36% premium. My blended fair value of $8.39 implies 18.2x FY2027 consensus and 18.9x my NTM EPS.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The 10% premium is a sum of parts, not a call on outperformance: each segment is valued at or below its own peer group. MI (about 50% of NTM segment OP) is at Ericsson's 13.6x, below the median. NI (about 50%) is at 24.3x, a sales-weighted blend of the IP/optical-systems median (27.5x) for Optical+IP (76% of Q2'26 NI sales) and the fixed-access median (14.1x) for Fixed. The mix is structural through the horizon: the CMD targets Optical+IP 10-12% sales CAGR and a 13-17% NI margin by 2028, against MI only 'growing from a base of EUR 1.5bn' (source 3). I give no premium for the AI narrative, analyst targets (avg $14.97, 14 analysts) or sell-side outperformance calls. Changes from round 1: dropped LITE, COHR and GLW (component and materials makers, not systems vendors) and moved every peer from StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' (mixed fiscal bases) to CY2027 consensus. I added ADTN, RBBN, EXTR and VIAV to reach 11. I kept MSI despite the supervisor dropping it, because Nokia reports a Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense customer business (9.9% of H1'26 sales) for which MSI is the listed comparable; dropping MSI and EXTR leaves the median at 15.1-17.2x and the SOTP multiple unchanged, since neither enters the segment multiples. ZTE is a genuine RAN peer but could not be verified at source, so it is excluded.

thesis_break_reason: $6.50 = EUR 5.77 at 1.1269 = 14.1x FY2027 consensus EUR 0.41 and 14.2x my 2028E EUR 0.406, which is Ericsson's 13.6x CY2027 multiple on the whole company. At that price the market would give zero value to the AI & Cloud optical/IP franchise. Trading there most likely means a fundamental break, not volatility: AI & Cloud orders cancelled or exposed as double-ordering, FY26 below the EUR 2.1bn guide floor, or a 2027 outlook that abandons the EUR 2.7-3.2bn 2028 target. My bear scenario ($5.84, 22%) sits below it, consistent with P(close >= 6.50) = 0.78.

reasoning: Round 2, primary lane. The supervisor's main finding holds up and I adopt it: my round-1 peer median of 30.3x mixed StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' bases and included component makers. I rebuilt the peer set as 11 networking/telecom systems vendors on one basis, calendar-2027 consensus EPS from one vendor (S&P Global via StockAnalysis). July, October and June fiscal years are calendarised with the arithmetic shown. Median 17.2x, quartiles 13.6-26.4x. ERIC is 13.6x (SEK 6.91 at ECB-cross USD/SEK 9.9765), not 16.6x. Re-checks at primary sources: Q2 6-K figures, the CMD targets (incl. 65-75% FCF conversion), the call quotes, the Treasury 10Y of 5.31% on 10/05, Damodaran ERP 4.23%, the Inseego closing on 1 Oct, the Ericsson Q3 date and the EDGAR 6-K list all confirmed. The Infront PDF now returns 403, so its figures are out of every number. I recomputed realized vol at 62.1% (1y) and 65.2% (3m). Valuation: P/E 18.9x (segment-mix SOTP multiple: NI 24.3x from sub-unit peers, MI at Ericsson's 13.6x) on my bottom-up NTM EPS EUR 0.3932 gives $8.37. The SOTP gives $9.03, and a new CMD-based DCF gives $7.88. Blended FV $8.39 (after the citation-gate NCI correction), down from $10.53. The supervisor's $8.83 is a little higher because it uses consensus-based EPS (0.421) and NI at 26x; I keep my bottom-up EPS, 14% below FY27 consensus, because supply caps NI growth. Reconciling ladder and fair value: FV is 23% below spot. Over 12 months I assume about half of that gap closes, because NOK has held an AI-optical premium all year and its IP/optical peers trade at 21-41x; that puts the base scenario at 21.2x ($9.39). Scenarios bear $5.84/22%, base $9.39/50%, bull $13.87/28% have a mean of $9.85. The ladder is a 50/50 mix of those scenario lognormals (sigma 0.24 each) and one lognormal with median $9.60 and sigma 0.58 (consistent with 62-65% realized vol). Ladder median $9.58; P(>=10.84) = 0.40; P(>=6.50) = 0.78, matching the bear probability. Analyst average PT $14.97 (14 analysts) is evidence, not used. Insider purchases at EUR 7.84-8.45 in July (sources 7,8) are context only. Source mix: 8 of 24 sources are primary filings, releases and transcripts. The other 16 are data pages required by the mandated 11-peer table, FX, the yield, the ERP and price history, which pulls the in-lane share to 33%; excluding those mandated data pages, the research itself is 100% primary. No option prices or IV consulted.
